reviewers.role: Prüferin (lizenzierte telc-B1-Prüferin): exam fidelity, rubric application, task clarity
Kursleiterin DaF/DaZ, Niveau B1.2: naturalness, level, didactics, scene plausibility

method: Both reviewers read every German string again. That covers start.folge (6 lines), the LS1 Rundschreiben (now 304 words), the LS2 Sitzung and the call (14 lines, 460 words), the 13 LS4 texts (SB2 letter with 172 words of body, 12 ads of 30–40 words), all input, structured, pool, reserve, cloze and check items, the LS3 rule table and end line, the micro-outputs, the Aussprache sources, the M3 task and model turns, the SA task (Frau Ottos 107-word mail with greeting and signature, the notes, the Leitpunkte, the 111-word model body), the redemittel, the story, the strategy cards, the facts and the Porträt. Every item was solved blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or the audio line and then compared with answer and accepted[]: 1 start gist, 10 input, 8 structured, 36 pool, 12 reserve, 5 cloze, 10 LV3, 10 SB2, 8 check items and 3 proof items. tb1.lv3, tb1.sb2, tb1.m3 and tb1.sa were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/tb1.json. The grammar ceiling was checked against registries/grammar-spine.json (falls b1.1-u06, um-zu-damit b1.1-u08, indirekte-frage a2.2-u03, praep-genitiv b1.1-u12, zu-infinitiv b1.1-u03, passiv-praesens productive b1.2-u06, sodass b1.2-u05, relativsatz-wer-was b2.1-u07). The lexicon was checked against b1.2/lexicon.json (40 u04 entries, 17 productive = 0.425) and level-profiles.json (b1.2: newPerUnit 43–48 ±10 %, productive 0.45 ±5 points, minutes.pruefung 30, ruleCardMaxWords 80). The can-dos were checked against registries/cando/b1.json, the cast against casts/a2.json, casts/b1.json and series.json, the rule cards against b1.2/rule-cards.json, the plan against b1.2/specs.json and curriculum/b1-2.json, and the Porträt fact against a web search (last coal train on 7 October 1992, flooding 1993–2000: claimDe holds). Each of the 11 r2 findings was re-verified. Validator: node scripts/course-v2/validate.mjs content/course-v2/b1.2/units/u04.json returned OK: 39 rules — 33 pass, 0 fail, 1 warn, 5 skipped; 0 blocker, 0 advisory. The one WARN is LEX-02 with a ratchet of 40, and all 40 notes read „recurs in 0 later unit(s)“. No lemma now occurs fewer than twice in the unit's inputs. The later-unit half cannot be measured while u04 is the only b1.2 unit file, so it is not logged as a unit finding. GRM-04 now passes with no advisory (r2 F11 closed on the rule side). node scripts/course-v2/check.mjs on the unit returned 0 errors.
verdict: Not exitable in round 3. The unit has moved a long way: 7 of the 11 r2 findings are fully fixed, two more are fixed on the unit side, and the validator is clean. The terrace plot now holds together (Frau Otto took the evening last week, asked about the terrace because the house was on Priya's list, and Herr Lehmann holds it until Monday, after Friday's Zwischenstand). The model mail relays Herrn Brandts request in the right register. l08's „das Einzige, was noch fehlt“ is true in its scene, tb1.sa is declared in the Prüfungsfokus and the chips, ls1-p06, ls1-p08 and the SB2 letter are repaired, every lemma occurs at least twice, and GRM-04 is silent. The exam layer is sound. LV3 has 10 situations, 12 ads and two x. SB2 has 10 gaps, 15 words and 5 left over. M3 and SA match tb1.json. Every key survived a blind solve, and no task copies a Modellsatz. Three MAJOR remain. (1) rc.brauchen-zu is unchanged for the third round (r1 F14, r2 F02), and the unit still shows it in LS1 and the Rückschau next to its own nicht/kein/nichts/nur teaching. This cannot be fixed inside the unit (sole-writer rule), so the orchestrator must route it to the rule-card owner before r4. (2) Three sentence-building items accept the rare split fronting „Zu bestellen brauche ich den Bus nicht.“ but reject the more natural whole-group fronting „Den Bus zu bestellen brauche ich nicht.“, which ls1-p06 accepts. (3) The proof item q02 („bestätigen bis ___“) rejects „Do.“, the normal abbreviation in a written note, although r2 asked for it. Six MINOR: the proof of nachricht-notieren links only the phone-number item and leaves q01/q02 orphaned; two lexical-recurrence insertions read unnaturally; Frau Otto asks whether the Seminarhaus called although LS2 had Priya write her a Gesprächsnotiz; LV3 06 depends on knowing that Dresden is in Sachsen; specs.json is still out of sync; LS4 still runs 35 min without an exam-time marker. Counts: 0 blocker, 3 major, 6 minor.

findings.path: content/course-v2/b1.2/rule-cards.json rc.brauchen-zu.de, .en (shown at steps[0].ruleCard and check.rueckschau[1]); vs steps[0].modelSentence, steps[0].structuredInput[2] (ls1-s03), steps[0].microOutput.promptDe, steps[1].input.lines[5] (ls2-l06), steps[2].ruleTable.rows[4], steps[2].endLine
findings.quote: Karte: „Ohne nicht oder nur benutzt man brauchen + zu nicht.“ / „Without nicht or nur, brauchen + zu is not used.“ · LS1-Mustersatz „Sie brauchen nichts selbst zu bezahlen.“ · ls1-s03 „Sie brauchen keinen Urlaub zu nehmen.“ · LS1-Mikro-Output „…, was niemand zu tun braucht.“ · LS3-Tabelle „nicht / kein / nichts / nur brauchen“ · LS3-Endzeile „… brauchen + zu mit nicht, kein, nichts oder nur benutzen.“
findings.problem: r1 F14 and r2 F02 are not fixed in the third round: rule-cards.json is byte-unchanged. Meanwhile the unit has moved further from the card. The LS3 table now also lists nichts, and the LS1 micro-output uses niemand. So the learner reads the card's absolute restriction in LS1 directly under a model sentence with nichts, then learns nicht / kein / nichts / nur in LS3, and meets the false rule again in the Rückschau. A rule-card simplification that has become false is a D error on a model surface (§9.4, §9.5). The unit author cannot close it, because rule-cards.json has another sole writer (§10.8). That is why it has survived three unit fix loops.
findings.fix: Rule-card owner, before round 4: replace the last sentence of de with „Das gilt auch mit kein, nichts oder niemand: Sie brauchen nichts zu bezahlen. Ohne Verneinung und ohne nur sagt man müssen.“ The card then has about 76 words, within ruleCardMaxWords 80; re-run GRM-05. en: „The same holds with kein, nichts and niemand. Without a negation or nur, use müssen.“ Add the table row [„kein / nichts / niemand … brauchen … zu“, „Sie brauchen nichts selbst zu bezahlen.“]. Orchestrator: assign this to the rule-card owner now rather than to the unit author. If the card is still unchanged at r4, treat it as a rail case under §9.4, because a 5th round cannot close a finding that sits outside the unit file.
findings.proposedRule: GRM-05 extension (as r2 F02): when a rule card states a licensing restriction (de „Ohne A oder B …“, en „Without A or B …“), every sentence that carries the card's spine point on a surface showing the card (the step's modelSentence and ruleTable rows, the check.rueckschau units) must contain one of the listed words. Fixture: rc.brauchen-zu × b1.2-u04 steps[0].modelSentence („nichts“).

findings.quote: ls1-p07 tiles „ich / brauche / den Bus / nicht / zu bestellen“, accepted incl. „Zu bestellen brauche ich den Bus nicht.“ — missing „Den Bus zu bestellen brauche ich nicht.“ · ls1-r02 tiles „du / brauchst / mich / nicht / abzuholen“, accepted incl. „Abzuholen brauchst du mich nicht.“ — missing „Mich abzuholen brauchst du nicht.“ · ls3-p08 tiles „Sie / brauchen / das Protokoll / nicht / auszudrucken“, accepted incl. „Auszudrucken brauchen Sie das Protokoll nicht.“ — missing „Das Protokoll auszudrucken brauchen Sie nicht.“ · ls1-p06 accepts „Ins Büro zu kommen brauchen wir am Freitag nicht.“
findings.problem: Each of these items accepts the rare split fronting, where the bare zu-infinitive is in the Vorfeld and the object is left behind („… aber selten“ in acceptedWhy). Each rejects the more natural fronting of the whole infinitive group with its object („Das zu erklären brauche ich wohl nicht.“ is an everyday pattern). A learner who has just been taught that the zu-infinitive can be fronted is more likely to build the group than the split form. The unit is also inconsistent with itself: ls1-p06 accepts whole-group fronting („Ins Büro zu kommen brauchen wir am Freitag nicht.“) only because the object sits inside the same tile there. A defensible answer that is rejected is MAJOR (§9.4). ls1-p07 and ls3-p08 are served in the pools, and ls1-r02 feeds requeue, Plateaus and the Einstufung.
findings.fix: Add „Den Bus zu bestellen brauche ich nicht.“ (ls1-p07), „Mich abzuholen brauchst du nicht.“ (ls1-r02) and „Das Protokoll auszudrucken brauchen Sie nicht.“ (ls3-p08) to accepted[]. For each, set acceptedWhy „grammatisch: der ganze Infinitiv mit zu steht im Vorfeld“ and reviewerConfirmed. The nur-items (c04, ls3-r03, ls1-p09) need no change, because there the group fronting would strand nur at the end („Das Formular auszufüllen brauchen Sie nur.“) and is not a natural sentence.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-09 / lib-validate/orders.mjs extension: when accepted[] contains an order with a zu-infinitive tile alone in the Vorfeld and an object tile in the Mittelfeld, the order with the object tile and the zu-infinitive tile fronted together („[Objekt] [zu-Infinitiv] V Subjekt nicht“) must also be accepted, unless the Mittelfeld keeps a focus particle (nur) that would be stranded. Fixtures: b1.2-u04 ls1-p07, ls1-r02, ls3-p08 (fail); ls1-p06 (pass); c04 (exempt, nur).

findings.quote: promptDe „Notiz für Emre – Elster-Reisen, Bus am 19.6.: bestätigen bis ___“ · audio „Bitte bestätigen Sie bis Donnerstag: 0341 47 11 30.“ · accepted [„Donnerstag“]
findings.problem: The item trains a written note, a genre that abbreviates. The prompt itself writes „19.6.“, and „Do.“ is the normal way to note a weekday. „Do.“ (and „Do“ without the point) is a correct answer, yet the item has no exact and no acceptedWhy for it, so the checker marks it WRONG. r2 F10 asked for „Donnerstag, Do. and bis Donnerstag“, and only the full form went in. q02 sits in the proof set of the unit's note-taking can-do, so a learner who takes the note well is marked down for it.
findings.fix: accepted: [„Donnerstag“, „Do.“, „Do“], with acceptedWhy „übliche Abkürzung für Donnerstag in einer Notiz“ and reviewerConfirmed. Keep the item free of exact, as now.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-07 extension: a notes / form_fill item whose answer is a weekday or month name must accept the standard German abbreviation (Mo., Di., Mi., Do., Fr., Sa., So.; Jan., Feb. …), with and without the point. Fixture: b1.2-u04-q02.

findings.quote: l13 „Kann ich ihr etwas ausrichten? Ich schreibe ihr gern eine Gesprächsnotiz.“ · l14 „Ja, gern. Für Ihre Gesprächsnotiz: Die Terrasse ist …“ · Rundschreiben „Sie können sich auch ohne Sitzung zu Wort melden.“
findings.problem: These are the r2 F09 recurrence insertions, and two of them read like lexicon quotas. On the phone nobody names the genre of the note the other person will write, and certainly not the caller („Für Ihre Gesprächsnotiz:“). „sich ohne Sitzung zu Wort melden“ mixes the meeting sense of the phrase (ask for the floor, as in l05 „Gut, dass Sie sich zu Wort gemeldet haben“) with the public sense, and the collocation „ohne Sitzung“ does not fit either. The German is grammatical, so this is isolated unidiomatic phrasing on an input (D 3), not an error.
findings.fix: l13: „Kann ich ihr etwas ausrichten? Ich lege ihr eine Gesprächsnotiz auf den Tisch.“ l14: „Ja, gern. Bitte notieren Sie: Die Terrasse ist …“ Keep `say` in sync. Circular: „Wer nicht in der Sitzung ist, kann sich auch schriftlich zu Wort melden: Dafür brauchen Sie nur eine kurze Nachricht an Frau Nair zu schreiben.“ (one sentence replaces two, and the brauchen-zu sentence stays). Re-run LEX-02: Gesprächsnotiz must still occur ≥ 2× in the inputs. If l14 loses it, the LS6 notes (Gesprächsnotiz, Anruf Herr Lehmann) or LS2 l11 („… und legen Sie Frau Otto bitte eine Gesprächsnotiz hin“) can carry the second occurrence.
